external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who borrows, renews and reserves books and uses self-service kiosks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
external_entities.notes: Members use the library app on phones and scan library cards at kiosks.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who handle loan problems and update member accounts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: All desk staff use the same shared login for the circulation page; individual users and branches cannot be identified.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: A phone application through which members request borrowing, renewal and reservation actions.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.
processes.notes: The app says which book and which member, or asks for a title.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API that handles loan operations and is the only component described as reading or writing the loans database.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: The Lending service note says: "The lending API is internal-only." The Interview transcript says: "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." These are conflicting positive claims about exposure. Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look." Authentication is therefore unknown. The API serves the circulation page and has no queue in front of it.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library card and books being borrowed or returned.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
processes.notes: What the kiosks talk to besides the lending API is not known.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: Priya corrected the earlier statement about two databases: "We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone." The lending API is the only thing described as reading or writing it.

data_flows.name: borrow book
data_flows.description: A member initiates a book-borrowing request through the library app to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member
data_flows.notes: The app's authentication behavior is uncertain: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."
data_flows.data_description: Book and member information for a borrowing request

data_flows.name: renew loan
data_flows.description: A member initiates a loan-renewal request through the library app to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Start with how a member actually borrows a book from their phone. … walk me through what happens when someone renews a loan
data_flows.notes: The API's authentication behavior is uncertain: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."
data_flows.data_description: Member and book information for a loan-renewal request

data_flows.name: reserve title
data_flows.description: A member initiates a reservation request through the library app to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Reserving is the same shape, the app asks for a title and the API puts the member in the queue for it.
data_flows.notes: The API's authentication behavior is uncertain: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."
data_flows.data_description: A title and the member's reservation request

data_flows.name: submit loan
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends a loan to the lending API after scanning it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan … to the lending API.
data_flows.notes: The kiosk protocol and authentication are not stated.
data_flows.data_description: A scanned book loan and associated library-card or member information

data_flows.name: submit return
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends a book return to the lending API after scanning it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.notes: The kiosk protocol and authentication are not stated.
data_flows.data_description: A scanned book return and associated library-card or member information

data_flows.name: extend loan
data_flows.description: Desk staff initiate a loan-extension action through the circulation page served by the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan
data_flows.notes: Desk staff use one shared login. The password is on a card taped under the desk.
data_flows.data_description: A loan-extension action for a member

data_flows.name: clear block
data_flows.description: Desk staff initiate clearing a block on a member account through the circulation page served by the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: or clears the block on the account
data_flows.notes: Desk staff use one shared login. The password is on a card taped under the desk.

data_flows.name: mark returned
data_flows.description: Desk staff initiate manually marking a book as returned through the circulation page served by the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned
data_flows.notes: The shared account records that the loan was closed by hand but cannot identify the person or branch.
data_flows.data_description: A manually recorded book return for a member's loan

data_flows.name: read and write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes member, loan and reservation records in the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.notes: The database protocol, authentication and transport encryption are not stated.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations and borrowing history

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which branch kiosks and desk staff work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.
trust_boundaries.notes: Desk staff are also stated to work on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data-centre zone where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The network over which phones talk directly to the lending API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.
trust_boundaries.notes: No modeled component is explicitly placed in this zone.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database is confidential because it contains names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: The Interview transcript explicitly states that these personal records live in the loans database.
